§12.2.3 Electrical Schematics

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

diagrams-electrical-schematics · images diagrams

✅ Normative

A component-level circuit schematic MUST use a faithful diagram/<language> encoding, preferring diagram/circuitikz, then diagram/tikz, then diagram/svg. If no suitable language can faithfully represent it, it MUST use a fenced description block. Every component symbol, designator, value, pin, terminal, net label and visibly drawn connection MUST be preserved.

Circuit diagrams.

The figure above is an IC functional block diagram rather than a component-level circuit; it follows Diagrams and Flowcharts§12.2.2, using diagram/plantUml, diagram/mermaid or another suitable language that preserves the printed blocks and signal connections. The component-level requirements below do not apply to a functional block diagram.

How the element is recognised

Component symbols joined by wires, usually with a reference designator and a value beside each one (R1 1Ω, C3 10μF). The way the components are oriented, and whether they sit in series or in parallel, is part of the content.

Preserve circuit meaning

The encoding MUST preserve component orientation, pins, junctions, crossings and series/parallel connections as drawn. An automatic graph layout that changes circuit meaning MUST NOT be used. Functional block diagrams use the block-diagram priorities in Diagrams and Flowcharts§12.2.2.

The fixed shape

When no suitable language can faithfully encode the circuit, the fallback uses a fenced description block (see Slide Diagrams§12.2.5).

  1. What it is — one line: Buck regulator input stage.
  2. Components — a list, one item per component in reading order (top to bottom, left to right): designator then value, both exactly as printed (R1 1Ω, C3 10μF). A component with no printed value is listed by its designator.
  3. Pins, terminals and nets — every printed pin, terminal and net label, verbatim.
  4. Connections — describe wires and junctions visibly drawn between identified parts. A crossing MUST NOT be treated as a junction unless the drawing marks it as one. Hidden or ambiguous connections MUST NOT be guessed.

Every printed designator, value and label is printed content and MUST be transcribed (never drop). Values MUST NOT be computed, normalised or corrected.
